title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
abstract: arXiv:2611.18514v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions. translated_title: 机制可解释性能否帮助解释大语言模型智能体的失败？——网页元素幻觉的案例研究
translated_abstract: 机制可解释性（MI）在解释大语言模型（LLM）的内部计算方面已取得显著进展；然而，这些进展尚未在解释基于大语言模型的智能体的决策过程方面展现出同等的成功。本文探讨了MI工具在应用于真实智能体失败场景时所面临的挑战。我们聚焦于其中一种失败：网页智能体幻觉出网站上不存在的操作。我们对与真实网站交互的Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct应用了一系列机制分析。我们发现，基于最后一个提示token训练的线性探针能够在生成开始之前预测幻觉（0.80 AUC），并且沿探针方向进行引导可以纠正85%的幻觉，但会干扰7%的有效操作。然而，这些结果仅能部分解释智能体为何产生幻觉：探针方向对提示格式非常敏感，因而丧失了大部分……
tldr: 本文首次将机制可解释性系统应用于网页智能体幻觉失败分析，发现线性探针可在生成前预测幻觉（0.80 AUC）且引导能纠正85%的幻觉，但由于对提示格式敏感，这只是一种部分解释。
en_tdlr: This study applies mechanistic interpretability to web agent hallucination failures, showing that a linear probe can predict hallucinations before generation (0.80 AUC) and steering corrects 85% of them, though this provides only a partial explanation due to sensitivity to prompt formatting.
